title: A parcel-lateness service: data, model, deploy, drift, retrain
summary: Data and a model before deploy; the service's own traffic and next month's parcels after. Every step is a real run of a cancho tool, and the seam where cancho-client-gen refuses ml-serve's OpenAPI document is shown as it is.
source: A recorded run of the real tools, replayed, on synthetic data (examples/late-parcels/make_data.py): nothing here measures a real courier.

steps.note: Data engineer: 400 parcels from last month. Three scanner dropouts have no distance; I drop them. peek counts the lines, header included.
steps.cmd: table --where "distance_km != ''" --format csv parcels.csv > clean.csv; peek --count-lines --lines 1:1 clean.csv | jsonq -p /data/total_lines --format text -

steps.note: Statistician: how far do parcels travel, and how many are late? (late is 0 or 1, so its mean is the late share)
steps.cmd: stats describe clean.csv --cols distance_km,late > desc.json; echo "distance_km mean $(jsonq -p /data/columns/0/mean --format text desc.json)"; echo "late share $(jsonq -p /data/columns/1/mean --format text desc.json)"

chart.title: Distance of last month's 397 parcels (stats' exact histogram)

steps.note: Data scientist: a logistic model for lateness, scored on the fifth of the rows ml holds out.
steps.cmd: ml fit --model logistic --target late --split train=0.8 --seed 1 --output late.ml clean.csv > fit.json; for m in accuracy recall roc_auc; do echo "$m $(jsonq -p /data/summary/holdout/metrics/$m --format text fit.json)"; done

steps.note: Deploy: serve the model. It answers on loopback, and /health says which model file it holds, by SHA-256.
steps.cmd:
ml-serve --model-file late.ml --port 18900 2> serve.log &
curl -s localhost:18900/health | jsonq -p /model_sha256 --format text -

steps.note: Asking it to listen on every address is refused unless a token file guards it.
A parcel (42 km, 5 pm, raining) is predicted late. A distance written as text is refused, and the refusal points at the field.
steps.cmd:
curl -s -XPOST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"distance_km":42.5,"hour":17,"rain":1}' localhost:18900/predict | jsonq -p /rows/0 --format text -
curl -s -XPOST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"distance_km":"far","hour":9,"rain":0}' localhost:18900/predict > bad.json; jsonq -p /rule --format text bad.json; jsonq -p /errors/0 --format text bad.json

steps.note: Frontend: I want a typed client from the server's own OpenAPI document. The generator refuses it.
steps.cmd: curl -s localhost:18900/openapi.json > openapi.json; clientgen openapi.json --python -o client.py; echo "exit $?"
steps.out:
clientgen: openapi.json: a schema is of no kind the model names
exit 1

steps.note: What did the server log? A line per request, never a payload. Three more calls, then count the statuses.
steps.cmd: for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s -XPOST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"distance_km":10,"hour":9,"rain":0}' localhost:18900/predict > /dev/null; done; tail -n +2 serve.log | tally --field 3 --delim ' ' | jsonq -p /data/top --format text -

steps.note: A month later. The rainy season: the parcels are not the ones the model learned from.
steps.cmd: for f in clean next; do stats describe $f.csv --cols distance_km,rain > $f.json; echo "$f: distance_km mean $(jsonq -p /data/columns/0/mean --format text $f.json), rain share $(jsonq -p /data/columns/1/mean --format text $f.json)"; done
steps.out:
clean: distance_km mean 25.157178841309825, rain share 0.33753148614609574
next: distance_km mean 36.12166666666667, rain share 0.6

chart.title: Share of parcels delivered in the rain
chart.short: Share of parcels in the rain

steps.note: The labels for the new month have come in. Score the model on all 300 new parcels.
steps.cmd: ml eval --model-file late.ml next.csv > next_eval.json; for m in accuracy recall; do echo "$m $(jsonq -p /data/metrics/$m --format text next_eval.json)"; done

steps.note: Retrain on last month plus the first 200 new parcels, and keep the last 100 aside to judge it.
steps.cmd: S=distance_km,hour,rain,late; table --select $S --limit 200 --format csv next.csv > next_train.csv; table --select $S --from 200 --format csv next.csv > next_test.csv; (cat clean.csv; tail -n +2 next_train.csv) > both.csv; for f in both next_test; do echo "$f $(peek --count-lines --lines 1:1 $f.csv | jsonq -p /data/total_lines --format text -) lines"; done

steps.note: Same 100 parcels, old model against the retrained one.
steps.cmd: ml fit --model logistic --target late --output late2.ml both.csv > fit2.json; for m in late late2; do ml eval --model-file $m.ml next_test.csv > $m.json; echo "$m accuracy $(jsonq -p /data/metrics/accuracy --format text $m.json) recall $(jsonq -p /data/metrics/recall --format text $m.json)"; done
steps.out:
late accuracy "0.83" recall "0.782608695652174"
late2 accuracy "0.89" recall "0.855072463768116"

chart.title: Accuracy: the old model against the retrained one

steps.note: Redeploy. A reload is a restart, and /health shows the model file changed.
steps.cmd:
ml-serve --model-file late2.ml --port 18900 2>> serve.log &
curl -s localhost:18900/health | jsonq -p /model_sha256 --format text -

steps.note: Reviewer: what may each tool do? The compilers proved it.
steps.cmd: for t in ml-serve ml table stats; do echo "$t $($t introspect | jsonq -p /authority/effects --format text -)"; done
